lessonRef.title: Concept model B: diversification across and within asset classes

focus: diversification across and within asset classes
objective: Compute the one-year outcome of a fictional equally weighted portfolio against single-asset alternatives, and quantify what diversification gave up and what it avoided.
scenario: The four simulated asset classes below are invented for this exercise, and the returns shown are the stated outcome of one simulated year rather than a forecast of any real market.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional one-year returns in these directions

tasks.directions: Over one simulated year, four fictional asset classes returned: a broad domestic stock fund 18%, a bond fund 3%, an international stock fund -6%, and a cash account 2%. A fictional investor has $8,000 and puts an equal quarter into each.

prompts.text: What is the return on the equally weighted portfolio?
What is the equally weighted portfolio worth at the end of the year? Round to the nearest cent.
What would the whole $8,000 have been worth in the broad domestic stock fund alone?

tasks.directions: Now find the worst single choice and measure the spread between the extremes.

prompts.text: What would the whole $8,000 have been worth in the international stock fund alone?
What is the spread between the best and worst single-asset outcomes?
How much did the diversified portfolio gain over the year?
How much did the diversified investor give up against the best single choice?

The diversified portfolio finished $1,100.00 behind the best single choice and $820.00 ahead of the worst. Explain what an investor is actually buying when they diversify, and say why the $1,100.00 is not evidence that diversifying was a mistake.

remediation: If the portfolio return comes out as 7.67%, the negative return is being left out of the sum altogether while the other three are still divided by 4. The international fund returned -6%, and at an equal quarter weight it pulls the average down. Add all four returns, including the negative one, before dividing by 4.
extension: Recompute the equally weighted return if the international fund had instead returned -20% and everything else was unchanged, and say whether the portfolio still finished the year positive.
